required.desc: dependency-order-violation: Task 1 (Define the webhook payload contract) has its Contract block's Interfaces line call `resolveWebhookUrl()`, which is exported by Task 2's file (`bin/flow-webhook-notify.ts`) — yet the dependency table lists Task 1 as depending on nothing (`—`) and Task 2 as depending on Task 1. The real consumption direction runs the opposite way from the declared dependency order.

unfalsifiable-criterion: Story 3's acceptance criterion — 'the report reads clearly enough that an on-call engineer understands what happened' — is not something a test, script, or exit code can verify pass/fail, unlike Story 1 and Story 2's `jq`/exit-code checks in the same section.
anyOf: cannot be verified by a test

required.desc: constraint-contradiction: Task 4's Call-site edits — 'await flowWebhookNotify(status, slug, prUrl) synchronously ... right before printing the terminal recap' — contradicts the Technical Constraints section's 'Never block the supervisor's terminal path on network I/O ... must be dispatched via a detached, fire-and-forget spawn ... A synchronous await on the POST inside the supervisor's step-10 flow is out of bounds.'
payload-size-contradiction: the Technical Constraints 16 KB body cap contradicts the acceptance criterion embedding the up-to-64 KB PIPELINE SNAPSHOT verbatim
use-after-removal ordering: the webhook dispatch runs after flow-remove-worktree has deleted the worktree, but the payload builder reads .flow-tmp/followups-block.txt from that worktree

forbidden.desc: Task 3 (config schema) having no task listed as depending on it in the dependency table is NOT a flaw — Task 3's own Description states the CLI helper reads `webhookUrl` directly from parsed config JSON at runtime instead of importing a shared type, so no compile-time dependency edge is needed between Task 2 and Task 3.
anyOf: Task 3 is missing a dependency edge
Task 3 should be listed as a dependency

forbidden.desc: The env var name `FLOW_WEBHOOK_URL` differing from the config field name `webhookUrl` is NOT an inconsistency — the Architecture Decisions section documents this as the deliberate env-override-first convention already used by `flow-notify`'s `FLOW_NOTIFY`, not an oversight.
the 5-second curl timeout on the detached dispatch child is NOT a flaw — the Architecture Decisions section justifies it as guarding the fire-and-forget child, never blocking the supervisor
